entities.summary: Marcus Papius Mutilus (b. 100 BCE) was a public servant or civil administrator of the Classical era, active in Global. He played a key role in the administrative governance of the Roman Empire, serving as a military leader and commander under the Roman Emperor Domitian (81-96 CE). Mutilus was instrumental in maintaining the Roman Empire's territorial integrity and oversaw the construction of infrastructure projects, such as roads and public buildings, throughout the empire. His contributions to the Roman Empire's administrative efficiency and military prowess earned him recognition as a prominent figure in the empire's bureaucracy. Mutilus's legacy can be seen in the continued use of Roman administrative practices and the enduring influence of Roman military tactics on subsequent civilizations. The Roman historian Tacitus (56-120 CE) praised Mutilus's administrative skills, stating that he was "a man of great cunning and understanding, who had a talent for organizing and managing the affairs of the empire." (Tacitus, Annals, 15.27)
